01
Session One

Looking Back

Ben McMahon

Session One opened with something important: gratitude. Before the numbers, before the strategy, Ben took time to reflect on what the team had actually built – and what clients were saying about it.

Client scores tell the real story: 9.1 average rating across seven responses from four client organisations, with 100% of events meeting objectives and 100% of clients saying they'd recommend Collaborate. "Fantastic on-site support. Your ability to bring our concepts to life is exceptional." That's VML & Ogilvy Japan on MWC 2026. That's what we're here for.

But winning doesn't mean pretending the last 18 months were easy. The session addressed the honest reality head-on.

"The endeavour and the hard work – my God, you guys work tirelessly. But I'm not up here asking you to work more. I'm asking you to work less, but smarter."

Ben McMahon – Kick Off 2026

Three structural challenges were named directly: the Middle East pipeline gap (a £11M+ shortfall as GCC client confidence froze in 2026), the reality of FoS and Automotive being biennial rather than annual revenue, and an infrastructure overhang – a business built for £25–30M operating on a £15M reality, burning approximately £478K in a single sprint on non-billing roles.

None of that was buried. The session owned it, then reframed it: a smaller, tighter, more creative Collaborate is not a lesser version of the business. The rebased target is £16M for 2026 – and the path back to profitability and joy is the same path.

Session Two

Moving Forward

Ben McMahon

Session Two set the direction. From the learnings of Sprints 3 & 4, five signposts were crystallised – the Collaborate constitution. The things that don't change, however the language evolves.

01
Client Centricity
If a decision doesn't improve the client experience – rethink it.
02
Creative Impact
We challenge convention. We push ideas. We don't decorate – we transform.
03
Collaboration as Culture
We win together. No soloists. Shared accountability, shared success.
04
Production Intelligence
The execution matters as much as the idea. Precision and impact are non-negotiable.
05
Agility in Action
We move fast, adapt quickly, communicate clearly. Process supports us – it doesn't slow us.

Alongside the signposts, the strategic rebase was announced: revenue target moves from £28M to £16M for 2026. Not a defeat – a decision. Targeted sales growth over volume. Fewer pitches, but pitched to win. Core client focus over chasing every brief. And agency-wide GP discipline, with 30% GP as the standard benchmark.

The tone was honest and energising in equal measure: "A lean, excellent, profitable business is a fun business."

03
Workshops & Spotlights

The Sessions

Andrew Walker · Phil Hodgetts · Chris Ambidge · Luke Daniels · Nina Boden · Lucy Bairner · Eloise Baker-Hunter · Lyndsey Sherriff

Three workshops ran across the afternoon, taking the main-stage themes into practical, interactive territory. The Core Workshop combined Phil Hodgetts' production update with Nina's Co-Lab Evolution – two complementary takes on how we work better together. Here's what was covered.

Workshop 01 · Agility AI Work Stream

Agility

Andrew Walker

Andrew Walker unveiled Agility – Collaborate's new AI intelligence platform, six months in the making. The starting point wasn't "what can AI do?" but "where should AI help us first, and what does it need to pay for itself immediately?"

The answer: win more, spend less, build smarter. With 73 pitches run in the past year, a 22% win rate, and 50% of those pitches resulting in zero revenue (jobs that vanished into thin air), the commercial case was clear. The pitch budget for 2026 was already exhausted by May.

Agility addresses this through a Sales Intelligence Engine – prospect monitoring, trigger event detection, and a connected data layer across HubSpot, Xero, Scorro, SharePoint and more, with Claude (Anthropic) as the umbrella intelligence layer. The session was live and hands-on: 45 people, 45 hours of testing in one afternoon.

Three layers of AI were mapped out: AI as analysis and intelligence, AI configured for specific tasks, and (on the horizon) AI agents working autonomously within defined boundaries. The ambition is clear – and the tool was live in the room.

Core Workshop · Production

Client Development through Project Delivery

Phil Hodgetts · Luke Daniels · Chris Ambidge

Phil Hodgetts presented a fundamental rethink of how Delivery and Production operate – titled "Client Development Through Project Delivery." The problem was named directly: two separate departments, separately motivated, with limited knowledge sharing or priority alignment. Resource efficiency suffers under commercial pressure, and leadership visibility suffers across both teams.

The solution: one integrated team built on shared accountability. Resources flex across accounts and projects based on skills and capacity – not departmental boundaries. Phil and Ross Oxenham (Head of Delivery) anchor the structure, with executive producers, project leads, coordinators and delivery managers forming a fluid, client-facing unit.

Every client gets a senior delivery team member as agency representative. Every project carries senior oversight with ultimate accountability for commercial success and client satisfaction. The goal is simple: fewer gaps, clearer ownership, and a team that clients experience as one joined-up unit rather than two.

Coming next: improved budgeting tools, AI integration into project management, and streamlined department reviews. The structural shift is the foundation – the tools and process improvements will follow.

Core Workshop · People

CoLab Evolution

Nina Boden

Co-Labs work. But they need to work for everyone – and right now, in some parts of the business, they simply aren't happening regularly enough. The session named the problem honestly before solving it.

Four barriers were identified: the admin burden of pre-meeting forms creating friction before conversations even start; a one-size-fits-all structure that doesn't reflect how different people actually work; competing priorities from 1:3:5s crowding out the real conversations; and confusing frequency leaving people unsure when they should be happening at all.

The evolution: 1:3:5s move out of Co-Lab space entirely – team targets and objectives belong at department level. Co-Labs now centre on what matters most: wins, challenges, blockers, and genuine development. Monthly 30-minute conversations replace the six-weekly hour, and the format is entirely flexible – a walk, a data deep-dive, a thinking space chat.

The biggest shift: transcription handles the admin. Turn on a transcriber, have the conversation, and the tool automatically captures everything under the right headings. AI then surfaces summaries and emerging development goals from your conversation history – so the record keeps itself. The three pillars going forward: Barrier-free · Purposeful · Personalised.

Workshop 03 · Sales & Marketing

New Business Workshop

Lucy Bairner · Eloise Baker-Hunter · Lyndsey Sherriff

The theme: People Buy From People. Warm connections and referrals generate up to 5x the engagement and 10x the response rates of cold outreach. New business isn't just a sales team job – it's everyone's job.

The session focused on two priority growth sectors: Tech and Automotive. Tech brands need physical experiences to make digital products feel human – think immersive demos, brand worlds, and storytelling environments. In Automotive, a massive shift is underway (EVs, software-defined vehicles, motorsport entertainment), creating year-round opportunities from launches to dealer experiences to PR events.

Teams worked through a "What's the Sell?" challenge across three angles – Creative Experience, Production Intelligence, and Agility & Partnership – exploring what problems we solve better than competitors and how we'd actually position ourselves in these sectors.

The practical ask: think about your network. Who do you know in tech or automotive – ex-colleagues, suppliers, LinkedIn connections, production partners, freelancers? Anyone connected to events, experiential, brand, marketing or innovation is a lead worth sharing. And use LinkedIn actively – talk about where you're working, what you're achieving, who you're working with.

And there's an incentive: £1,000 is up for grabs for anyone whose introduction leads to a new brief, RFQ or RFP worth over £50k from a brand new to Collaborate. T&Cs to follow – but the message is clear. We all have a network. Now's the time to use it.
